entities.summary:
Nicolaus Ragvaldi was the Bishop of Växjö and Archbishop of Uppsala in Sweden from 1438 to 1448. He played a significant role in the Gothicist tradition, which sought to reform the Catholic Church in Scandinavia. Ragvaldi's influence extended to the Swedish Parliament, where he advocated for the rights of the clergy and the nobility.

As the Archbishop of Uppsala, Ragvaldi was responsible for the governance of the archdiocese, which included the cities of Uppsala, Linköping, and Örebro. He also oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries throughout the region.

Ragvaldi's legacy can be seen in the continued importance of the Gothicist tradition in Swedish art and architecture. His efforts to promote the rights of the clergy and the nobility also had a lasting impact on the development of the Swedish Parliament.

In conclusion, Nicolaus Ragvaldi was a key figure in the Gothicist tradition, whose influence extended beyond his own lifetime to shape the course of Swedish history.
